description: Emotiveness benchmark fixture for benchmarks/tts-emotion.ts. Ten scenes excerpted verbatim from the sides in test_data/, each listed in full so the AI director judges every target line from its real context, as in production. `targets` name the lines that get rendered and rated; each carries a hand-written ground-truth label: `emotion` (what a good reader would play), `family` (one of the audit's emotion families), `intensity` (low/medium/high), `cue` (where the script signals it: none = plain dialogue, dialogue = the words themselves, stage = a stage direction before the line, parenthetical = an explicit delivery parenthetical), and `reply` (whether it answers the line before it). The targets mix intensities on purpose — eight are labelled neutral and over half are low-intensity — because a flat read is most audible on the quiet, ordinary lines, and an over-played one on the same lines. `quick` marks a 20-line subset for cheap iteration. Voices are ElevenLabs catalog names, resolved to ids at run time.

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.direction: Robby flips on a light to wake his parents, Sam (40s) and Linda (40s), as if a bugle playing Reveille.
lines.text: Satellite GPS estimates Bolsa Chica Ecological Reserve is a 23 minute drive. We should leave in 22 minutes to arrive 15 minutes early for the 8AM Guided Tour.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.direction: Linda gently opens her eyes. Sam barely budges.
lines.text: 10AM hike, Rob. Remember? To get more sleep.

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.text: 8AM is ideal to see the Plovers most active. I’m already dressed. Next is teeth brushed.

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.direction: Robby scampers into the bathroom. Linda tosses off the covers.
lines.text: We’ve come a long way.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.direction: She slides out of bed. Sam resigns and sits up.
lines.text: Okay, 8AM it is! Early bird catches the worm... right, Rob?

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.direction: Robby ignores Sam. He addresses Linda. His mouth can barely keep up with his brain as he squirts paste on his toothbrush.
lines.text: Mom, did you know the Western Snowy Plover raises up to three broods per year where the season is long, like here in California. The female deserts her mate when the chicks hatch and initiates a new breeding attempt with a different male.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.direction: Linda shoots Sam a playful glance: Interesting... Off this, Sam gets up and wraps his arms around her.
lines.text: Don’t get any wild ideas, mate.

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.text: 21 minutes until departure!

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.text: Our chick needs to feed, mate. You wanna try? I have granola bars.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: I’ll grab something from the coffee shop. I need caffeine.

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.text: Not a minute later!

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.text: You heard him.

scenes.heading: INT. CAR - RENTAL HOME - PARKING LOT - DAY

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.direction: Robby is near melt-down. We see the clock on his phone: 7:22. Linda soothes him from the driver’s seat. No sight of Sam.
lines.text: We need to leave now, Mom!

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.text: Dad’ll be back any minute, Robby.

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.direction: Robby’s clock turns: 7:23AM. He grunts and flails his arms.
lines.text: I’m going to miss the plovers when they’re most active!

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.direction: Robby rocks back and forth in his seat. Linda spots Sam, approaching with a coffee cup and paper bag.
lines.text: Dad’s back! We’re leaving now.

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.direction: Linda turns the key, waves: Hurry it up! Sam picks up his pace.
lines.text: We’ll still be there fifteen minutes early, Robby.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.direction: Robby softens, off reassurance and the engine’s familiar hum. Sam pulls open the door and hops in the passenger’s seat. Linda ignores him, checks her mirrors. Sam checks his phone: 7:23.
lines.text: Sorry, Rob. There was a long line. Got your bagel!

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.direction: Sam offers Robby his bagel. He refuses; calmer, yet eyes still glued to the time. Sam gives up and offers Linda coffee. She shakes her head, and turns to Robby.
lines.text: Robby, what do plovers eat?

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.text: Mainly terrestrial and aquatic invertebrates.

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.text: Are they as active if they miss a meal? Are you?

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.direction: Robby grabs the bagel from Sam. Linda puts the car in drive. Sam takes a sip of his coffee and stares out the window.
lines.text: Linda: 1, Sam: Goose-egg. Again... Lonely in this pigeon-hole.

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.text: Not now.

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.direction: Thunder disturbs Robby. He shakes in his chair, notebook pinned to his chest. Linda and Sam observe him from the bed, quietly.
lines.text: If we take him back there tomorrow, we’ll have to switch our flight and pay a change fee.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: It’s worth it.

lines.speaker: LINDA
lines.text: What if he finds out something’s happened?

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: We’ve come a long way. Right?

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.direction: Linda smiles at Sam’s echo of her earlier sentiment.
lines.text: Call the airline?

lines.speaker: ROBBY
lines.direction: Linda gives Sam a kiss: You got this. She leaves the door ajar, exits. Sam joins Robby, now rocking in his chair.
lines.text: Same time tomorrow. 15 minutes early. I need to help Ruth protect and preserve again. Can’t be late.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: We’ll be there, Rob. No coffee runs this time, promise.

scenes.heading: INT. CANNED! CORP HQ - BULLPIT - NIGHT

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.direction: Attractive women line up along each cubicle. They carry trays of refreshments for the men. Carl is still trying to take off the bracelet. Ethan walks over from his cubicle up front. He too has an electronic bracelet, though his has a longer leash.
lines.text: It’s pointless. You’ll never get it off...unless you quit.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: What? Quit? No. I’m not a quitter. I just. I have to use the bathroom.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: Use a bottle.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Seriously?

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: Seriously.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: What if I have to shit?

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: Don’t eat solid food.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: You’re kidding, right?

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: I’m as serious as our sales target, which you’re already behind, by the way. We are here to sell not soil ourselves so if you can’t control your bladder or pucker your asshole then maybe you don’t have the can-do attitude required.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Oh no, I can.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: Can what?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Can do?

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: That’s the spirit! My name’s Ethan, senior manager. My job is to make sure you do your job. Do you know what that is?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: The Secretary said I’ll get my assignment soon, so, I’m guessing it’s whatever that is.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.direction: (makes a buzzer sound)
lines.text: Wrong! Your job is to sell cans, and not just any cans. You sell CANNED! Cans. The best cans. Do you know who invented the tin can?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Nicolas Appert.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: Ding, ding, ding. That’s right! And, what did Nicolas Appert do?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: He was a chef. He fed people.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: Not just any people; soldiers. The tin can was invented so soldiers during wartime would have the sustenance they needed to kick ass. That is what we do.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: I get it. We provide sustenance to all the people out there fighting to make it in life.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: No! We. Kick. Ass. We are soldiers, and the war we fight is for the dream.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: What dream?

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: The only dream that matters. The dream that keeps this country running 24/7, 365: The American Dream. Do you believe in that dream?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: I do.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: Then get to work.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Yes, sir.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.direction: Ethan extends a hand. He and Carl shake.
lines.text: It’s getting late. What about my family?

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.text: You’re a part of the company now. We’re your family.

lines.speaker: ETHAN
lines.direction: Ethan goes back to his cubicle.
lines.text: Alright, men! We just sold two million cans in five hours! It may be armageddon out there, but it’s Aloha-geddon in here!

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.direction: The women set down their trays and take off their skirts to reveal they are wearing hula skirts. The women start hula-dancing. The Bull Pit men cheer.
lines.text: What the hell is this place?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.direction: Joey, who is in Cubicle 6, looks over and sees Carl is frightened.
lines.text: Hey, man. I’m Joey. What’s your name?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Carl.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Nice to meet you, Carl. I know it can seem like a lot at first. I was just like you are when I got here three weeks ago. My advice: Relax, hit your numbers, and enjoy the show.

scenes.heading: INT. CANNED! CORP HQ - BULLPIT - LATER

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.direction: Joey drops to one knee in front of Caity. She says yes. Everyone cheers except for Carl.
lines.text: What is happening?

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.direction: The Secretary overhears Carl. She turns her attention to him.
lines.text: What’s happening is your corporate brother has just found his work wife. You should be celebrating like your colleagues. Instead, you are sitting there, not doing anything. You think you can just sit there and do nothing?

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Your numbers are the lowest of all.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Well...

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Where is the report on the new product? It has been weeks since I gave it to you.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Right here, ma’am.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.direction: Carl hands the Secretary a binder. She opens it and flips through the report.
lines.text: What is this crap? This isn’t what you were assigned to do. You were assigned to make the new product launch ready.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: I figured that it would be in the best interest of the company if a safety analysis was performed, and it’s a good thing I did it, because the product is potentially dangerous. The parts are cheap. There’s no way to prevent it from accidentally turning on, or launching the blade. People could cut themselves, or worse.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Worse?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: Death. I think people could die if we release this product. We should conduct proper testing in a controlled environment.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.direction: Carl watches with worry as the Secretary walks into the CEO’s office and then returns with something in her hands. She brandishes the item in front of his face.
lines.text: This is the CANNED! Can Can-Opener. Now, you’re telling me that this could be dangerous?

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.direction: The Secretary turns on the device. A motor vibrates. The two inch circular blade spins. The Secretary holds the blade close to Carl’s neck.
lines.text: You want tests?

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.direction: Carl tries to back away but he hits the wall. The Secretary creeps closer.
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: This is a controlled environment, one you do not control.

lines.speaker: CARL
lines.text: I understand.

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.direction: Beverly rises up from her chair, but is tipsy, so she has to hold onto the chair for support.
lines.text: I want to give thanks to our beautiful host and hostessesss-

lines.speaker: J.T.
lines.text: You’re supposed to say what you’re thankful for, not give thanks to-

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.text: I am THANKFUL to be here with many of the people I love. I am THANKFUL for our surprise guest.

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.direction: (turning drunk sad on a dime)
lines.text: I am so, so, so thankful to share this Thanksgiving with Eddie. I-- it’s been really hard for me this year, without Annie. So I can only imagine what it’s been like for you...

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.direction: She sobs and stumbles a little, J.T. letting out an annoyed sigh at her drunken display.
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: J.T.
lines.text: This is supposed to be a celebration not a-

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.text: You know what I am most thankful for, J.T.?

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.direction: (steps/stumbles towards him)
lines.text: That next Thanksgiving I won’t have to sit across from your miserable fucking face.

lines.speaker: EDDIE
lines.direction: Raises her glass to toast, no one joins her, so she lowers her glass to the table, thud. Shamed silence fills the room. J.T. is turning bright red in embarrassment as Beverly plops down, eyes filled with tears. Eddie notes the confusion on The Orphan’s face.
lines.text: Oh, man, sorry, I should have caught you up earlier, so you could join the conversation.

lines.speaker: EDDIE
lines.direction: Points to Beverly and J.T.
lines.text: J.T. and Beverly--as you have probably figured out--should be divorced, but J.T. needs Beverly’s health insurance cause he’s got cancer.

lines.speaker: J.T.
lines.text: Woah!

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.text: Eddie?

lines.speaker: J.T.
lines.direction: J.T. turns his ire to Beverly.
lines.text: You told him?

lines.speaker: BEVERLY
lines.text: You’re not the only one this is difficult on.

lines.speaker: J.T.
lines.text: I’m sorry, is my cancer ruining your Thanksgiving?

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Silas Jenkins, 50, thin, with skin burned black by the Florida sun, hair solid white and rumpled, sits by a pot-bellied stove sliding a whiskey bottle into the corner, tin cup in hand.
lines.text: Tobias MacIvey! It gets a mite chilly on the river in early morning, a’ little fire feels good.

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Tobias slaps at his arm.
lines.text: Skeeters. Skeeters have a way of findin’ ya anywhere ya go. Not much unlike hungry people.

lines.speaker: TOBIAS
lines.direction: Tobias looks around to see the shelves are mostly bare. He’s only got a few words, not in the mood for Silas’ liquid cheer.
lines.text: I got over fifty good coon skins, and I c’n promise more on credit.

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Silas coughs a little and slaps his leg.
lines.text: FIFTY coons!? Man you done cleared out ever’ critter down this side of the Mason Dixon!

lines.speaker: TOBIAS
lines.direction: Tobias turns to him, hopeful.
lines.text: Made a new kind a’ coon trap.

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Tobias gets lost in the emptiness of the store and turns to Silas concerned.
lines.text: Course you did, course you did. You a good man, Tobias. Smart one.

lines.speaker: TOBIAS
lines.text: Need supplies, food.

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Silas takes an over-dramatic sigh and sets down his cup to get serious.
lines.text: I got bad news, Tobias. Some Reb soldiers come in here a few weeks ago ‘n took darn everything I had. Flour, sugar, cornmeal, bacon, salt.

lines.speaker: TOBIAS
lines.text: Coffee?

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.text: That too. I ain’t got one blessed thing left to trade.

lines.speaker: TOBIAS
lines.direction: Tobias deflates.
lines.text: We’re in a spot, now. Need somthin’

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: He scans the store.
lines.text: Ah, I’m sorry, Tobias. Even the Reb soldiers ain’t got uniforms to wear, it’s a blockade! N’less you c’n grow wings and fly over the Union line. Hell, I ain’t et nothing for three weeks now but mullet.

lines.speaker: TOBIAS
lines.text: Well, I don’t recommend the hogs neither, but I c’n shoot critters.

lines.speaker: TOBIAS
lines.direction: Tobias eyes the whiskey bottle.
lines.text: Any powder and shot?

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Silas catches his drift.
lines.text: Ah, well you know I’m good for somethin’ Gotta keep a few... necessities.

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Silas sips then hobbles up, becoming more animated. He pops a loose plank and rummages past some clanking whiskey bottles. He pulls one topside and places it on the floor in front of Tobias.
lines.text: Take a nip if ya like. Helps in the hard times.

lines.speaker: SILAS JENKINS
lines.direction: Silas pops his head up, buzz setting in.
lines.text: It’s a fish. Just a fish with teeth. And it ain’t very good.

lines.speaker: LOLLY
lines.direction: Lolly (40s), in a party gown and Louboutin heels, stumbles out of the vestibule door and lands on the carpet, all the while managing to hold an open bottle of Veuve Cliquot. Not one drop spilled. Behind her stands Andrea (40s). The sight of Lolly on the floor sends her into a fit of drunken laughter. (laughing)
lines.text: I think I’m smattered.

lines.speaker: ANDREA
lines.text: Smattered? As in small and tattered?

lines.speaker: LOLLY
lines.direction: (laughing)
lines.text: No, No. I mean, I mean, mean... I meant to say smmmasht, with a T-

lines.speaker: ANDREA
lines.direction: Lolly stops short. Her eyes go wide with fear. She brings her hand to her chest, frightened. (suddenly sober)
lines.text: What? What’s wrong?

lines.speaker: LOLLY
lines.text: I... I think I’m having a heart attack.

lines.speaker: ANDREA
lines.text: Was it the gummy?

lines.speaker: LOLLY
lines.direction: (panicked)
lines.text: CAN GUMMIES DO THAT???

lines.speaker: ANDREA
lines.direction: She drops her hand and lies down on her back, trying to slow her breathing. Andrea spots Lolly’s phone sandwiched between her breasts. It illuminates as it vibrates. (howling)
lines.text: It’s your phone, your phone.

lines.speaker: LOLLY
lines.text: My wha?

lines.speaker: ANDREA
lines.direction: Andrea bends down, awkwardly in her fitted dress, and answers the phone without removing it from Lolly’s chest. She speaks into her breasts, which makes Lolly erupt in laughter. (sophisticated)
lines.text: Hello? It’s Lolly’s tatas speaking. How may they help you?

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.text: This thing. This whatever it is. You and me. Do you think this is normal?

lines.speaker: TOM
lines.text: I don’t know. Who cares about normal?! I’m happy. Aren’t you happy?

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.text: You’re happy?

lines.speaker: TOM
lines.text: You’re not?

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.text: All we do is argue!

lines.speaker: TOM
lines.text: That is such a lie!

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.text: This can’t be a total surprise. I mean, we’ve been like Sid and Nancy for months.

lines.speaker: TOM
lines.text: Summer, Sid stabbed Nancy seven times with a kitchen knife. We’ve had some disagreements but I hardly think I’m Sid Vicious.

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.text: No-- I’m Sid.

lines.speaker: TOM
lines.direction: (beat)
lines.text: So I’m Nancy?!

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.direction: The Waitress comes out with the food. Tom and Summer stop their discussion until the meal is served and the Waitress leaves. Summer starts to eat.
lines.text: Let’s just eat and we’ll talk about it after. I’m starving.

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.direction: Without another word she goes back to her pancakes. Tom watches her eat like this is the worst travesty in the history of mankind. (mouth full)
lines.text: Mmm, you’re so right. These are great!

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.direction: Tom looks at his food in disgust. He may never eat again. (innocent)
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: SUMMER
lines.direction: Tom stands up to go.
lines.text: Tom, don’t. Come back. You’re still my best fr---

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.direction: Midge, now in her nightgown, hair and make-up still evening perfect, comes out of the bathroom. She sees something and stops in her tracks.
lines.text: What are you doing?

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.direction: Joel is stuffing clothes into a suitcase on the bed. He looks at her and stops.
lines.text: I have to go.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.direction: Midge stares at him confused.
lines.text: I have to leave.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.direction: Midge stares at him still confused.
lines.text: You. I have to leave you.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.direction: Beat.
lines.text: That’s my suitcase.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: It is?

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: You’re leaving me with my suitcase?

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.direction: Joel looks at the floor.
lines.text: But... tomorrow’s Yom Kippur. Joel?

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: I’m... I’m not happy.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: No one’s happy. It’s Yom Kippur.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: I don’t know how to do this. I’m not good at things like this.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: Things like what? Like leaving me?

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: Well, then don’t. Practice a little. Do it later when you’re more confident about the moves.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: Midge...

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.direction: (pleading)
lines.text: Joel... the rabbi’s coming.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: I know he is.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: Five years we’ve been trying to get the Rabbi. This year, we got him. We got the Rabbi!

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: I should go.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: No. Please. I don’t understand.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: I thought my life was going to be something different. I thought I was going to be someone different. But tonight was just so terrible... I mean, a room full of people just watching me bomb...

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: It was one stupid night...

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: He got more laughs in five minutes than I did in five months.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: You’re jealous of the Rabbi? He was in Buchenwald! Throw him a bone!

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: Did you ever think you were supposed to be something and then you suddenly realized you’re not?

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: Yes. Married.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: I’m never going to be a professional comedian, Midge. Never.

lines.speaker: MIDGE
lines.text: Well... of course not.

lines.speaker: JOEL
lines.text: What do you mean “of course not”?

label.emotion: quiet pride, said half to herself
affectionate teasing, mum running the morning
dry, amused: backing the kid up
gentle redirect, a question to calm him
factual recitation, a kid reciting what he knows
self-deprecating, a little hurt under the joke
warm promise to a frightened kid
warmth with something chilling under it
quiet menace with a blade at his neck
apologetic, warming to his own grievance
defensive, scared of where this is going
